Incident Summary - Duplicate Tracking Numbers, Ironbridge Logistics Platform
Date: Mar 8 | Severity: SEV-2

A counter-reset bug in the tracking-number generator caused 62 shipments to be assigned tracking numbers that were already in use by other active shipments, between 02:00 and 02:40 UTC.

Impact: Customers looking up one of the 62 duplicated numbers saw the wrong shipment's status for up to 6 hours before the issue was caught by a customer service escalation, not automated monitoring.

Root cause: A database failover at 01:58 UTC caused the tracking-number counter (an in-memory value) to reset to its last-checkpointed value instead of its true last-issued value, a gap of about 400 numbers that then got reissued.

Fix: Counter now persists on every increment instead of periodic checkpoints; failover-safe as of Mar 9 deploy.

Postmortem: Appointment Scheduling System Outage
Incident ID: INC-771 | Solace Health Platform | Date: Mar 15
Authors: Aleksander Brandt, Simone Laurent

Summary
Between 07:00 and 09:15 UTC, the patient-facing appointment scheduling system was completely unavailable, returning connection errors for all requests. Phone-based scheduling (a separate system operated by clinic staff) was unaffected and used as a fallback.

Timeline
- 06:55 - A routine database maintenance window begins, expected to take 10 minutes with no downtime (online index rebuild).
- 07:00 - The index rebuild unexpectedly takes an exclusive lock on the appointments table, blocking all reads and writes.
- 07:02 - Scheduling system starts returning connection timeout errors as requests queue behind the lock.
- 07:05 - On-call engineer Simone Laurent is paged.
- 07:10 - Simone's initial hypothesis: an application-layer bug, since the maintenance window was expected to be non-blocking.
- 07:25 - Simone escalates to Aleksander Brandt after ruling out an application-layer cause.
- 07:40 - Aleksander identifies the database lock and determines the index rebuild's "online" mode silently fell back to a blocking mode because the appointments table exceeded a size threshold undocumented in the database vendor's tooling.
- 08:00 - Killing the rebuild job is considered but rejected, since partially-built indexes could leave the table in a worse state; the team decides to let it complete instead.
- 09:15 - The rebuild completes; the lock releases; scheduling system recovers immediately with no further errors.

Root cause
An index rebuild tool's "online" mode silently used a blocking strategy once the table exceeded an undocumented size threshold, and no monitoring existed to detect a long-held table lock in progress.

Impact
Patients could not book, reschedule, or cancel appointments online for 2 hours and 15 minutes. Clinic staff fielded an estimated 340 phone calls during this window, roughly triple the normal volume, but no appointments were missed or lost - phone scheduling covered all requests, just with longer hold times.

Action items
1. Add monitoring for long-held table locks with automatic paging - owner: Aleksander, due Mar 22.
2. Test index rebuilds against a production-sized table copy before running on production going forward - owner: Simone, due Mar 29.
3. Document the vendor's undocumented size threshold internally and file a bug report with the vendor - owner: Aleksander, due Mar 20.

What went well
Phone scheduling as a fallback meant zero missed appointments despite the 2+ hour online outage.

Quarterly Report - Marigold Finance Core Ledger Migration
Q1 | Sponsor: Rowan Blackwood | PM: Ivy Sorensen

Executive summary
The core ledger migration to the new platform remains on track for the June 30 cutover. Parallel-run testing (old and new systems processing the same transactions side by side) began Feb 1.

Parallel-run results
Through March, 340,000 transactions have been processed in parallel. 339,650 matched exactly between old and new systems (99.9%). The 350 mismatches were all traced to a rounding-rule difference in fee calculations for a specific account type (business overdraft accounts), which affects roughly 2% of the customer base.

Fee rounding fix
Engineering has identified the fix: the new system needs to match the old system's round-half-up behavior for this account type specifically, rather than the new system's default round-half-even behavior. Fix is coded and in testing, targeting deployment by Apr 15, well before the June 30 cutover.

Budget
Approved budget: $5.2M over 14 months. Spend to date: $3.4M, on track against a $3.5M planned-to-date figure.

Risk register
1. (High) If the rounding fix introduces any new discrepancy class, the parallel-run clock effectively restarts for affected account types, which could threaten the June 30 date. Mitigation: fix is being tested against 3 months of historical overdraft-account transactions before redeployment to parallel-run.
2. (Medium) Regulatory sign-off is required before cutover; the regulator has requested the parallel-run achieve 99.95% match rate (not yet met) sustained for 60 consecutive days before they'll review the cutover request.
3. (Low) Two engineers rotating off the project in April for a prior commitment; backfill hiring is in progress and not yet a blocker.

Compliance note
The 99.95% regulatory threshold is stricter than the team's own internal target of 99.9%, which has already been met. Reaching 99.95% specifically requires resolving the rounding-rule mismatches described above.

Next steps
Ivy to deploy the rounding fix by Apr 15 and restart the 60-day sustained-match clock immediately after. Rowan to brief the board that June 30 depends on hitting 99.95% by roughly May 1 to leave room for the regulator's review window.

Stakeholder note
The regulator's account team has been briefed informally on the rounding-rule fix and did not raise concerns about the approach, though their formal review only happens once the 60-day sustained window is complete. Ivy plans a follow-up briefing once the fix is live in parallel-run, well ahead of the formal 60-day clock restarting for the affected account types.
